cohorts.summary: Initial players encounter broken settings menus and movement key issues.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the keybinds menu in the settings as broken, reporting that changing movement keys does not function properly.

citations.review_text:
Without going into detail, the keybinds section of the settings page is probably the buggiest menu I have ever seen in a video game. What is most frustrating about it is that the game tells you there is a way to rebind your keys, but that feature just plain doesn't work (only for some keys, oddly enough), which makes me doubt whether it was even tested. There were also other reports of this issue on the Steam forums, but none of them were addressed yet.

I'm sure the game itself is great, but until the issue is resolved I'll be keeping this review negative for visibility. If you too want to play on mouse and keyboard with a non-WASD layout, I can't recommend this game.

changing keybinds on keyboard just doesnt work, unplayable, not *truly* accessible. 
im left handed and i use my left hand on my mouse  and my right on keyboard and because of this i cant use wasd comfortably, and instead of using arow keys, i usually use, "L" for forward "." for backward and "," and "/" for left and right and as of me writing this you can only change w and d. with a and  s can be unbinded but not changed and there is no indication of WHAT you changed the key to.(specifically for movement) as soon as you try and change the backwards key it changes to the forward key, same goes for the move left key too it will change to the move right key. and all while you are try to change wasd, wasd is just permanently useable and workable entirely in its normal state.(unless you unbind a and s) w = forward a = left s = backward and d = right and if  you unbind a and s it changes to w and s being forward and  a, d being move right. there is no way to make the dialog move slower, and or move to the next part on ONE'S command rather than it auto progressing(im a slow reader and as if i was reading outloud in my head) but that is going off of the "hey wake up" volume and gamma part. so as of now i am unable to play this cool game.

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players praise the free release, diverse art styles, and multiple story routes.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game offers multiple routes or endings to experience.

citations.review_text:
After replaying the first chapter MANY times, as well as buying the supporter edition and unlocking bonus content, I feel the need to write an in depth review of it.
First of all, the artstyle is just gorgeous man. Like genuinely the smallest of details like the moving texture on the characters to the 3D/2D hybrid stuff, it all just blends to create this like, perfect mix of something visually appealing while still being really experimental, and on that note,
THIS GAME IS TRULY SOMETHING ELSE.
People don't call this the weirdest game they've ever played for nothing man, holy hell.
Even being an ENA fan from the webseries before I played the game, nothing could actually prepare me for what the hell this was. You could easily tell there's a lot of LSD Dream Emulator and Yume Nikki influence by just one playthrough of it.
The gameplay itself is quite good as well. A first playthrough generally might take a couple hours just to solve the base puzzles (or maybe I'm stupid), but on replays they go by pretty quickly and it's never like, a chore to play this game, if you know what I mean? Like, yes, there's two routes you can take, both resulting in the same ending, and no there's no real incentive to replay them if you don't care about achievements or anything, but it's like, why not? Why not replay the game to see the other route? It doesn't take that much time. Why not buy the supporter edition and support the incredible talent behind this game? Replaying the game to find the dogs isn't that hard, and it doesn't cost that much. Why not try for every achievement (except the one where you jump across the bridge on the white river without the humanboard that one sucks)? MOST of them aren't hard. Like, this is a VERY well crafted experience to play.
And THE SOUNDTRACK DUUUUUUUDE.
Now I make music myself so I might have a liiiiiittle bit of bias here, but oh my god this game's soundtrack is an absolute masterclass. Oliver Buckland, METAROOM, and everyone else involved absolut…

The setting and concepts of this game feel revolutionary to gaming. It genuinely feels like the most truly creative and original game I've ever played, with a captivating storyline and multiple endings to the chapter. I replayed it several times and recommended it to friends, and I love the candid-style dialogue of a lot of the characters. The characters are very individualized with distinct personalities and languages, phrases, voices/tones of talking, even down to the characters used in subtitles. Aside from just being great in specific aspects, the gameplay and storyline are captivating, immersive and engaging. I cannot get enough of this game and can't wait for future chapters to come out.

[b][h1]ENA: Dream BBQ[/h1][/b]This feels like less of a game and more of an art project, It contains so many varying art mediums with it's 3D world, 2d characters and animated cutscenes, they shouldn't work together so well but everything in the game is so surreal that it all fits right in.

[b][h2]Gameplay[/h2][/b]There's not a huge amount to do gameplay-wise, it has some interesting elements but you're more so just exploring the surreal world that has been built and trying to follow the nonsensical story. It's better to just try and experience this game blind.

[b][h2]Achievements (14/14)[/h2][/b]The majority of the achievements are missable and require tasks to be done in a certain order and you can easily skip past some. It's much easier with a guide.

[b][h2]Music/sound[/h2][/b]To add to this game's bizarre nature, all characters are voiced in a variety of different languages, but subtitles are on by default. The game also has some really unique music.

[quote][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/39729435-JHG-Reviews/?appid=2218750]Check out my Curator page[/url][/quote]

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features voice acting in multiple different languages.

citations.review_text:
I've no joke seen an unfathomable amount of clips and edits for ENA: Dream BBQ, but when I finally got around to playing it, I couldn't believe how enjoyable and funny it was. The animations, character writing, use of different languages for voices, and level design gives this game a quality and vibe I haven't encountered in any other game to date. Highly recommended, and you'd be doing yourself a disservice by not at least trying it.

Digital horror and existential crises with a sprinkle of 90's computer nostalgia fricking rocks, and don't let anyone tell you otherwise. That includes TADC too :)

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game is available for free.

citations.review_text:
When people say "games are an art form," this is exactly what they mean. ENA: Dream BBQ feels more like an interactive, absurdist movie than a  traditional game, and I absolutely loved it. It's FREE on STEAM, BY THE WAY (which is absolutely criminal), so there's no excuse not to try it.

The visuals pull heavily from retro games mixed with early internet vibes, giving you pure nostalgia. I also adored the fourth-wall-breaking interactions with the characters. I believe the lore is actually really dark, but since I didn't know what was happening for most of the game, I have to say it was perfect.

I do need to add that the only bad thing about this game is that having a j*b cuts into playtime, but it's manageable.

Now that I found out ENA is a YouTube series, I'm on my way to watch it.
fun little story game, crazy that this is free.

Kind of boring honestly, still it’s free and has creative visuals so if this looks like your cup of tea then give it a shot. But if you feel like this will get boring after a while then it probably will. I feel like the game is insisting on some deeper ideas but those ideas are either not as interesting as people say they are or not there at all. Since this game is free and short I will give it a positive rating, since it’s not costing people anything to just try it.

Edit: Watching the youtube video version of this and honestly it's much better format than this. Easier to take in everything that's happening when you're not the one in control. It's easier to set pace for the audience as well, which is crucial for these kind of vibe based experiences.
